note: defeq_collapse means the statement's two sides reduce to each other at default transparency. That is a CANDIDATE signal, not a verdict: it fires both on vacuous definitional restatements AND on genuine finite computations, because reduction is how a concrete computation is proved. The discriminator is whether the operands are hand-entered constants or actually computed -- spot-checked, most in this batch are hand-entered tables (jonesAtOne is a table whose torusLink2 entry is marked 'placeholder'; klEigenvalueAtOne and pairCount are two separate `Int := 2`).

scaling_note: maxRecDepth and the COMMAND's own 200000-heartbeat budget both bite on long module lists (fine at 8, fail at 15); the driver now sets maxRecDepth 100000 and maxHeartbeats 0. Even so, throughput is the binding constraint: batch at ~8 modules. Follow-up: the 7 previously-timed-out modules were retried at batch size 3 -- 3 completed in 4m14s, the remaining 4 still time out at 560s. Batch size alone does not rescue the heaviest modules; those need their own budget.
compile_note: Olean coverage was the binding constraint, not the analysis. scripts/lean/compile-cone.sh resolves a module's QOU import cone depth-first and compiles the leaves first -- `lean -o` on a module whose imports have no olean simply fails, so a missing module cannot be built in isolation. Mathlib is never rebuilt (a `lake build` would EVICT the restored cache, qou-r13s). Measured: 8 previously-uncovered modules compiled and analysed here. Second compile round: 7 of 8 targets built; QOU.BraidKnot.JHopfQOneProvenance and QOU.BraidKnot.JonesNuclearQuotient FAILED to compile even with a 420s per-module budget -- a compile failure, distinct from the kernel-pass timeouts.

batch5_note: Batch 5 (2026-08-27): QOU.Mathlib.PermutationEnumeration, run SOLO -- 73 theorems, 58 collapses (79 %), the highest rate in the sample. TWO findings, and the second is the more important. (1) OPERATIONAL: this module had exceeded every batch budget tried and was recorded as unreachable. It completes alone in well under 2400 s. The constraint was the BATCH, not the module -- a batch shares one elaboration and one heartbeat budget, so a single heavy module starves the rest and the whole command dies. Run heavy modules solo rather than declaring them out of reach. (2) CALIBRATION, and it inverts the natural reading of the collapse rate: 79 % here is ENTIRELY LEGITIMATE. `coxeterLength perm := (univ.filter (fun p => p.1 < p.2 and perm p.1 > perm p.2)).card` is the real inversion-count definition over Mathlib's `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`, so `coxeterLength (s1*s2*s1) = 3 := by decide` enumerates every pair, filters by inversion and counts. It CANNOT be arranged -- a wrong permutation product gives a wrong count. Compare QOU.Mathlib.WenzlBridgeConcrete at 62 %, where the collapses ARE the defect (conjugate-duality lemmas between two defs spelled identically). SO THE COLLAPSE RATE IS NOT A QUALITY SIGNAL, in either direction. The discriminator, stateable now from two measured extremes: does the collapsing computation TRAVERSE A REAL STRUCTURE (a Finset.filter over a permutation group, a Kauffman bracket reduction, a factorial), or does it UNFOLD TWO DEFS THAT WERE SPELLED IDENTICALLY? The first is a computation; the second is a restatement. Note that `local_only` does not separate them either -- the coxeterLength_* group is local_only and legitimate, while permutationCount_n_five is FOREIGN and equally legitimate. What separates them is what the local def DOES.

coverage.note: QUOTE THIS BLOCK, NOT A BARE MODULE COUNT. The kernel pass has seen 51 of 2257 QOU modules -- 2.3 % of the tree, 3.4 % of what currently has an olean. It is a SAMPLE and the file name says so; nothing here supports a corpus-wide claim about how common defeq collapse is. CORRECTION: PR #5875's scope section said "8 modules still lack oleans". That 8 was scoped to the modules carrying UNADJUDICATED MAJOR FINDINGS at that moment, not to the corpus -- the real figure is 741 of 2257, a third of the Lean tree. Reported as a corpus number it invites the reading that coverage is nearly complete when it is 2.3 %. Same error class as the precision-figure correction one commit earlier (a filtered count published as an unfiltered one), made twice in one session by the agent auditing the corpus for it. The 741 are not all failures: most have simply never been asked for. Two are known compile failures at a 420 s budget (QOU.BraidKnot.JHopfQOneProvenance, QOU.BraidKnot.JonesNuclearQuotient); the rest are untried. scripts/lean/compile-cone.sh reaches any of them without letting `lake build` evict the restored Mathlib cache.
